title: Possible Revisions to Schemes Following Government's Study on Impact of Divorce
what_it_is: Possible Revisions to Schemes Following Government's Study on Impact of Divorce

sections.label: Divorce study and next steps
sections.summary: The MSF study on inter-generational effects of divorce covered over 100,000 children, about 8,800 with parents divorced before they were 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development arising from the Study on the Inter-generational Effects of Divorce on Children in Singapore (a) whether there were significant differences in the outcomes of the children based on the age of the child when the parents got divorced; and (b) what are the Ministry’s next steps in further examining the issue of a "divorce penalty" on our children and studying the efficacy of our interventions to reduce the effect of this penalty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The MSF study on the inter-generational effects of divorce covered more than 100,000 children and of these, about 8,800 of them were children whose parents divorced when they were below 21 years old.

sections.label: Divorce and children outcomes
sections.summary: The study findings show a significant negative association between parental divorce and children outcomes based on five factors analysed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The study findings show a significant negative association between parental divorce and children outcomes based on the five factors analysed.

sections.label: Children in Between attendance
sections.summary: About 6,500 children a year have parents who divorce, but only about 100 children attend Children in Between.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Although there are about 6,500 children a year whose parents get divorced, only about 100 children attend “Children in Between”.

sections.label: MSF rebates for programmes
sections.summary: MSF offers a rebate of $140 for the PREP workshop, or $70 for other approved programmes by Social Service Agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MSF offers a rebate of $140 for the PREP workshop, or $70 for other approved programmes conducted by Social Service Agencies.

sections.label: Bersamamu and Marital First Responders
sections.summary: Since July 2019 about 6,000 couples attended F2F Bersamamu, and since March 2019, 215 community, religious and lay leaders were trained as MFRs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Since Bersamamu started in July 2019, about 6,000 couples have attended the F2F Bersamamu with their Kadis/Naib Kadis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Since March 2019, we have trained 215 community leaders, religious and lay leaders as well as marriage solemnisers as Marital First Responders (MFRs).

sections.label: Supervised visitation court orders
sections.summary: In 2019 there were 249 Court Orders for supervised exchange or supervised visitation out of 7,620 divorces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As a rough gauge, there were 249 Court Orders for supervised exchange or supervised visitation in 2019 – I guess you could consider that these are high-conflict situations – out of 7,620 divorces.

sections.label: Compulsory marriage parenting programme
sections.summary: The marriage parenting programme for civil divorces is a compulsory consultation session for parents with minor children before they file for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The marriage parenting programme I mentioned earlier for civil divorces is a consultation session for parents with minor children before they file for divorce and it is compulsory.

sections.label: Studying divorce causes and marriage strengthening
sections.summary: MSF will study the suggestion, explore what causes divorces, and focus on strengthening marriages and helping couples contemplating divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I guess, in any situation, we also have to consider the family dynamics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But I think it is a worthy suggestion the Member has made and MSF will study it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Are there any plans right now for this kind of research to further pursue the factors contributing to these outcomes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I think with the data we have on hand, the next step we will look at is to explore what causes divorces and how we can better protect and strengthen marriages and also to mitigate the impact of divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If we were to attempt to try to explain causality, the way we would approach the study would be very different from how we have done so for this particular study because we would have to track the experience of the child from when the divorce takes place and we have to be able to isolate specific factors and, over time, see how the child has grown and developed and what eventually the outcome of the child is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, for us to undertake that kind of longitudinal study to determine causation will require a lot of resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I think, for the time being, we will focus efforts on how we can better strengthen marriages, help the process when couples are contemplating divorce.
